quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Most motorcycles:

options.text: Have brakes on both the front and rear wheels.
Have three brakes: front, rear, and emergency brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have brakes on both the front and rear wheels.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes. One brake controls the front wheel, and one controls the rear wheel.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle:

options.text: Expect it to handle the same as your own bike.
The owner will check the brakes for you.
Leave extra space between you and other vehicles so you have time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave extra space between you and other vehicles so you have time to stop.
questions.explanation: Before riding a borrowed motorcycle, do the same safety checks you would do on your own bike. Ride carefully on an unfamiliar motorcycle and keep extra distance between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: When stopped behind another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Get as close as possible to the vehicle.
Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
Look for chances to squeeze through stopped traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay back from the vehicle in front of you, even when both of you are stopped. This gives you room to escape if that vehicle backs up or if another vehicle comes too fast from behind.

questions.question: Motorcycle riding gloves are often:
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: An approved helmet:

options.text: Lets you see clearly to the sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you see clearly to the sides.
questions.explanation: An approved helmet allows you to see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding. Approved helmets have labels showing the maker's name, instructions, and the safety standards they meet.

questions.question: Which surface is NOT slippery?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces have poor grip for tires: wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers in the road. Dry pavement is safer for motorcyclists.

questions.question: Before riding, check your tires for all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check the air pressure, tread depth, and general wear of your tires.

questions.question: If you feel tired while riding, you should:

options.text: Keep riding and hope you wake up.

questions.explanation: Do not ride when tired. On long trips, take a rest break at least every two hours to prevent fatigue.

questions.question: Motorcycles have blind spots like cars. When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
Slow down so vehicles in your blind spot can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which of the following should you check before riding?

options.text: The wear and tread of your tires

questions.correctAnswerText: The wear and tread of your tires
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your motorcycle thoroughly. Inspect tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, taillight, turn signals, brake light, clutch and throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding next to parked cars?

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
Other drivers may be going slowly while looking for a spot.
The road surface may be uneven.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
questions.explanation: Riding next to parked cars is dangerous. A driver might pull out without looking. Car doors may open into your lane and people may step out from between cars.

questions.question: What material gives the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather gives the best protection for motorcycle riders. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs completely when riding.

questions.question: Why should you not ride directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: You may be in its blind spot.
It is distracting to have a vehicle next to you.
Other drivers may want to use the lane.
It would be hard to see what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly next to another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in the driver's blind spot. The driver will not know you are there. The vehicle could also block your escape path if danger appears.

questions.question: What should you NOT check on your tires?
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire air pressure, tread, and general wear. You do not need to check flexibility.

questions.question: What does smooth downshifting allow you to do?

options.text: It should not be done near other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Smooth downshifting lets you use engine braking to slow down. If you use engine braking, turn on your brake lights separately so other drivers know you are slowing.

questions.question: How can you reduce your risk of an accident?

options.text: Ride within one foot of the vehicle in front of you.
Use your signals only when you feel like it.
Stay alert and be ready to avoid a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay alert and be ready to avoid a crash.
questions.explanation: To reduce accident risk, be visible to others. Use signals, brake lights, and proper lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and to the sides.

questions.question: What is the most important thing you can do to survive a crash?

options.text: Wear a quality helmet that is fastened securely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a quality helmet that is fastened securely.
questions.explanation: Wearing a quality helmet that is fastened securely is the single most important thing you can do to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. These regulatory signs tell drivers what rules to follow.

questions.question: Which type of clothing helps other drivers see you?
questions.explanation: Wear gear that makes you visible to others. Bright, reflective clothing makes it easier for other drivers to see you.

questions.question: For the best protection, a helmet should:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state standards. It should fit snugly around your head with no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of a crash, you should:

options.text: Keep your intentions unknown from other drivers.
Always stay within a foot of another vehicle.

questions.explanation: Be visible to other drivers at all times. Use your signals and brake light. Keep space around your motorcycle. Scan the road ahead, behind, and next to you.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast:

options.text: Is acceptable as long as you stay under the speed limit.
Is safer on a motorcycle than in a car.
Is acceptable as long as no vehicles are near you.
Can cause you to end up in another lane or leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause you to end up in another lane or leave the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast is dangerous. You may not be able to hold the turn and could drift into another lane or off the road. Take turns slowly.

questions.question: A motorcycle operator can slow down by:
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists can slow down by downshifting. Be aware that downshifting does not turn on the brake lights.

questions.question: When checking tire pressure:

options.text: Eyeballing the tire is a good method.
It is best to squeeze the tire.
Compare the height of the tire to another tire.

questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check tire pressure before every ride. A tire may look fine even if it is under-inflated, so looking at it is not enough.
